LVGLab 0.8.0 helps with components that have several top-level objects and makes the start page easier to use.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64), installer | `LVGLab-0.8.0-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows 10/11 (x64), portable | `LVGLab-0.8.0-windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux (x64, glibc 2.35+) | `LVGLab-0.8.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `LVGLab-0.8.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (Intel) | `LVGLab-0.8.0-macos-x64.tar.gz` |

The Windows installer adds a Start menu entry and can associate `.lvglab` files. The archives need no
installation: unpack and start `lvglab` (`lvglab.exe` on Windows). Check downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
On macOS, run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine lvglab` once if the unsigned binary is refused.

## New

- **Components with several top-level objects**: an instance is made of the first top-level object only, so a
  second object next to it (for example a divider) never showed up on the screens. The component list now warns
  about this, and **Group them** puts all top-level objects into one container. The container is as large as the
  objects together and the objects sit inside it at fixed offsets, so it can be resized (for example to a height
  of 80 px) without the content moving out of view.

## Fixed

- Start page: the whole row of a recent project reacts to the pointer. Before, only the gaps between the texts
  opened the project and highlighted the row.
